the steroid-induced LH surges in guinea pigs are associated with a coordinated increase in the proportion of LHRH/FoS neurons in rostral, but not caudal, LHRH neuronal populations.

the steroid-induced LH surges in guinea pigs are associated with an increase in the number of LHRH cells that express Fos and a loss of LHRN immunoreactivity in terminals in the median eminenence, consistent with augmented release of LHRH.
the induction of Fos within LHRH cells is more prominent in rostral, rather than caudal, forebrain regions during the LH surge in steroid- treated guinea pigs.

delineating relationships among subgroups of LHH neurons during the steroid-induced LH surges of laboratory rodents.

the induction of the Fos protein within LHRH cells in relation to the LH surge in the guinea pig.

the induction of Fos in LHRH neurons appears to be more prevalent in LHRH neuronal subgroups that are located rostrally and are involved with the regulation of the LH surge in the guinea pig.
the induction of Fos in LHRH neurons is a dynamic process that is not uniform across the LHRH neuronal population, and is related to the steroid-induced LH release.

the steroid-induced LH surges in ovariectmized guinea pigs are not mediated by the activation of the majority of LHRH neuronal subgroups, but that a subset of LHRH neuron subgroups are activated in surging guineas pigs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LHRH neurons that are activated by steroid treatment in guinea pigs are a subpopulation of the total population, and the subpopulation is not uniform in terms of the degree of Fos expression.
the LHRH system is a dynamic network of neurons, with the expression of LHRH mRNA and LHRH peptides being regulated in a complex manner.

the induction of Fos within LHRH cells is a dynamic process, which varies with respect to time of day, stage of the estrous cycle, and steroid milieu, and is influenced by the presence of other neurochemicals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are distinct subgroups of Luteinizing hormone releasing hormone (LHRH) neurons in guinea pigs, and that these neurons have different responses to the steroid-induced LH Surge.
the induction of Fos within LHRH cells during the LH surge is not restricted to LHRH cells in specific brain regions or to a particular subset of LHRH cells.
there is a coordinated increase in expression of the immediate early gene Fos in a subset of LHRH-containing neurons in the forebrain of surging guineas pigs.
